text:
Ana M: Heads-up — my feature branch feature/vpc-routing is red on CI after rebasing onto main. Failing only on this branch. CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/teams/infra/pipelines/9023
CI Bot: pipeline #9023 run 1: failed (integration-e2e-us) — see job logs: https://ci.redwood.example/teams/infra/pipelines/9023/1
Kyle T: Which job/test is failing specifically? can you paste the failure and the job name
Ana M: job: integration-e2e-us (matrix node 3). Failing tests: tests/integration/connectivity/connectivity_tests.py::test_vpc_peering_timeout. Error snippet:
```
E   AssertionError: Expected status 200, got 504
requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: Read timed out
...
```
Ana M: I retried the pipeline twice and still red. Locally `pytest -k connectivity` passed though.
Jamal R: Could be a subtle env change from the rebase. Did any dockerfile or infra config get modified in the commits between main and your branch?
Ana M: I checked diffs; only app code touched. No obvious docker changes.
Sophie L: Sometimes the CI parallelization exposes timing/race issues. Two quick options: bisect to find the commit that broke it, or run the failing job with `--no-cache` and longer timeout.
Sophie L: Suggested bisect commands:
```
git fetch origin
git bisect start HEAD origin/main
# run the failing test locally as part of the bisect command
git bisect run pytest tests/integration/connectivity/connectivity_tests.py::test_vpc_peering_timeout -q
```
Kyle T: Also check logs for `gcloud auth` timeouts — those cropped up in recent CI flakes. Maybe a credential or region var got overwritten.
Eve (infra): I kicked a rebuild with increased job timeout and forced no-cache on docker build for run 4: https://ci.redwood.example/teams/infra/pipelines/9023/4 :wrench:
CI Bot: pipeline #9023 run 4: started
Ana M: Thanks @Eve, queued run 4
CI Bot: pipeline #9023 run 4: failed — same test failing (ReadTimeout)
Jamal R: I'll take a quick bisect locally, I have a branch set up with the intervening commits.
Jamal R: Quick update — bisect narrowed it to commit 7a9b3f2 (auth/retry tweak in vpc-manager). Reverting that commit locally makes the e2e pass repeatedly.
Ana M: Nice find, thanks @Jamal. I pushed a temporary revert branch and triggered CI: branch revert/vpc-retry-rollback -> pipeline #9030
CI Bot: pipeline #9030: started
CI Bot: pipeline #9030: succeeded :tada:
Ana M: Green. I'll open a formal PR reverting the problematic change and add a targeted E2E to catch the timeout case. Also will include the bisect steps and the bad commit hash in the PR description.
Kyle T: Please include the local repro commands and the `--no-cache` run info, that'll help infra if this resurfaces. :+1:
Sophie L: Also mark the test with @flaky for now and add an issue to harden the env isolation in CI.
Ana M: Done — created PR #4348 (revert vpc retry tweak) and added a follow-up issue. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :pray:
